articles.title: Georgia's Sirish Subash Wins Top Young Scientist Title for AI Pesticide Detector
articles.excerpt: The 14-year-old Indian-origin ninth grader's handheld device PestiSCAND detects pesticide residues on produce with over 85% accuracy, earning him the 2024 3M Young Scientist Challenge's $25,000 grand prize.
articles.nri_angle: The win extends a strong run of Indian-origin students dominating American STEM competitions, mentored and rooted in a diaspora family's values.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Skyroot's Pawan Chandana Named to TIME100 Next 2026 After Vikram-1 Orbital Triumph
articles.excerpt: The Skyroot Aerospace co-founder and CEO joins TIME's annual list of 100 emerging global leaders, months after his company's Vikram-1 became the first Indian private rocket to reach orbit.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S rocket ahead of its Mission Prarambh suborbital flight in November 2022, which paved the way for the Vikram-1 orbital triumph
articles.nri_angle: Pawan Chandana's TIME100 Next listing spotlights India's private space sector — built by engineers who stayed in India — as a new destination for diaspora aerospace talent and global investment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, Earns Third Guinness Title as Youngest Woman Grandmaster
articles.excerpt: Guinness World Records has officially recognised the Indian-origin British prodigy as the youngest chess player ever to earn the Woman Grandmaster title, following her performance at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin British schoolgirl Bodhana Sivanandan, daughter of Tamil Nadu parents, earns her third Guinness World Records title — a point of pride for the British-Indian community and diaspora worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bricks Hurled at Ohio Hindu Temple During Prayers, Windows Shattered
articles.excerpt: The Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights was struck around 1:30 pm on Friday while priests and devotees were inside. No arrests have been reported, and surveillance footage is under review.
articles.image_caption: Shattered glass lies scattered across the floor inside the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir after the attack. The Richmond Heights, Ohio temple was struck with bricks on Friday afternoon while priests and devotees were inside.
articles.nri_angle: The attack targeted a place of worship for Hindu Americans in Ohio during prayers, sharpening community fears about temple safety and the response to anti-Hindu hate in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: RCMP Arrests Five in Extortion Probe Targeting British Columbia Car Dealership
articles.excerpt: The coordinated arrests followed a year-long RCMP investigation, Project E_PURSUANCE, into extortion demands, arson and shootings targeting an auto dealership's co-owners in Surrey and Langley.
articles.image_caption: An RCMP officer; the force arrested five in an extortion probe targeting British Columbia car dealerships.
articles.nri_angle: The arrests mark the first major break in a year-long wave of extortion targeting British Columbia's South Asian community, whose members police are now urging to cooperate as the investigation widens across Western Canada.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Faruk Patel Built a Rs 10,964 Crore Green Energy Empire From Rs 1 Lakh
articles.excerpt: The son of a bus conductor who once drove an auto and worked at Pizza Hut, Dr Faruk G. Patel built KP Group from a Rs 1 lakh trucking venture in 1994 into one of India's leading solar and wind conglomerates.
articles.image_caption: Faruk Patel, who built a Rs 10,964 crore green energy empire from Rs 1 lakh.
articles.nri_angle: UK-based writer Imtiaz Patel Varediwala's biography of Patel (in English, Gujarati and audiobook) gives diaspora readers a documented playbook of a first-generation Indian entrepreneur — and a model for investing back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shabana Azmi, Naseeruddin Shah Join Mumbai Protest Demanding Election Chief's Ouster
articles.excerpt: Thousands gathered at Shivaji Park for the Cockroach Janta Party's demonstration seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral-roll irregularities.
articles.image_caption: Protesters gather at Shivaji Park in Mumbai during the Cockroach Janta Party demonstration on October 2. Veteran actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi and singer Vishal Dadlani joined the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
articles.nri_angle: The protest over electoral-roll integrity resonates with NRIs who closely follow the health of Indian democracy and have family members voting back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Newsom Appoints Indian American Ajay Bhutoria to California Engineering Board
articles.excerpt: The Fremont tech leader and former Biden AANHPI commission member will serve as a public member of the California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors and Geologists.
articles.image_caption: Ajay Bhutoria, Indian American technology executive and civic leader from Fremont, California. Governor Gavin Newsom appointed Bhutoria as a public member of the California Board for Professional Engineers, Land Surveyors and Geologists.
articles.nri_angle: Bhutoria's appointment puts a prominent Indian American immigration advocate — a champion of green-card backlog relief and H-1B reform — in a California regulatory leadership role.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Go Home' Row Escalates: Krishnamoorthi Doubles Down as Dhillon Reveals Daily Racist Attacks
articles.excerpt: What began as a Florida councilman's 'take your curry and go home' jibe has widened into a bipartisan reckoning, with Trump's civil rights chief disclosing identity attacks and new data showing half of Indian Americans report discrimination.
articles.image_caption: US Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi speaks at a podium.
articles.nri_angle: The episode has become a defining test of belonging for Indian Americans, the community repeatedly targeted in the Florida councilman's remarks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Diwali Returns to London's National Maritime Museum With a New Bazaar
articles.excerpt: The free 'All Together Now' festival on 7 November adds a Diwali Bazaar of South Asian designers to a programme of performances, workshops and talks in Greenwich.
articles.image_caption: Dancers in red and white traditional dress perform at the National Maritime Museum's Diwali celebration as a large crowd looks on. This year's festival, All Together Now, runs on 7 November and adds a first-ever Diwali Bazaar to the free day-long programme.
articles.nri_angle: The festival is aimed squarely at Britain's Indian and South Asian communities, with programming — food talks, identity panels, sustainable fashion — that reflects how the diaspora keeps Diwali today.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tech Mahindra and Infinite Uptime Partner to Scale Physical AI in Manufacturing
articles.excerpt: The deal pairs Infinite Uptime's PlantOS™ prescriptive-intelligence platform with Tech Mahindra's global IT-OT transformation capabilities, targeting steel, cement, chemicals, and mining — first in North America and Europe.
articles.image_caption: Tech Mahindra is partnering with Infinite Uptime to scale physical AI in manufacturing.
articles.nri_angle: A Pune deep-tech startup scaling worldwide via an Indian IT services giant, with Indian engineers in North American and European manufacturing plants among the first to encounter the joint offering — a marker of Indian IT climbing the AI value chain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mizoram's Anthurium Festival Returns After Three Years With Flowers, Culture, Adventure
articles.excerpt: The October 1–3 event at Ailawng and Reiek blends flower shows, treks, cave exploration and Mizo heritage — and the state is pitching it as tourism that puts villages first.
articles.image_caption: Performers in traditional Mizo dress do the Cheraw bamboo dance at the Anthurium Festival venue, the festival sign visible at left. The festival returned to Ailawng and Reiek villages in Mizoram Mamit district on October 1, 2026, after a three-year hiatus.
articles.nri_angle: For the Mizo diaspora at home and abroad, the festival's return is a cultural homecoming signal — and its women-led anthurium export story gives diaspora travellers a point of pride and a reason to plan visits around it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Bombay Students Begin Hunger Strike, Demand Accountability in Sahil Wakode's Death
articles.excerpt: Weeks after second-year student Sahil Wakode was found dead in his hostel room, students at IIT Bombay have begun a hunger strike demanding a credible investigation into allegations of caste-based harassment and a biased internal probe.
articles.image_caption: Sahil Wakode's parents sit on a hunger strike holding his portrait, beneath a banner reading "Hunger Strike Day-4, Justice for Sahil". They allege he faced caste-based harassment at IIT Bombay and are demanding action against those named in the police complaint.
articles.nri_angle: NRI families track IIT campus accountability closely; the case tests whether elite Indian institutions offer transparent probes and external oversight that diaspora parents expect.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: EaseMyTrip Gives Hero Flydubai Pilot Free Domestic Flights for Five Years
articles.excerpt: After Capt Smit Machchhar was stabbed by his co-pilot on Flydubai flight FZ1073 and helped save 170+ lives, EaseMyTrip announced free domestic travel for him, his wife and children for five years.
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian pilots fly for Gulf carriers, so the attack on Capt Machchhar in a flydubai cockpit on a Gulf–Tel Aviv route hits close to diaspora families in the UAE; his heroism has resonated globally as a story of composure saving 170+ lives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Civil engineer earns Rs 35 lakh from four acres of red bananas
articles.excerpt: Abhijeet Patil of Maharashtra skipped the engineering job queue in 2015, planted red bananas in 2020, and sold 60 tonnes through Reliance and Tata outlets in three metros.
articles.image_caption: Red bananas fetch Rs 60–90 per kg, several times the price of the common yellow variety.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs investing in Indian farmland get a template: premium horticulture with organized-retail linkages beats commodity crops, and professional skills transfer to farming.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After 20 Miscarriages Over a Decade, Chicago Mom Celebrates Son's First Birthday
articles.excerpt: Ranim Haddad, 36, of Alsip, Illinois, endured at least 20 pregnancy losses with husband Fuad before conceiving naturally in 2020 — and marked the milestone on October 1, the start of Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month.
articles.image_caption: A mother holds her newborn; a Chicago mom is celebrating her son's milestone after a decade-long fertility journey
articles.nri_angle: Recurrent pregnancy loss is a subject many South Asian families also face in silence, where cultural pressure around having children can make fertility struggles especially isolating — the Haddads' openness gives other families permission to name their own losses.
tags: Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Factory Floor or Family Office: India's Young Heirs Choose a New Path
articles.excerpt: A $1.5 trillion succession wave is under way, and a new generation would rather allocate capital than run the family business — worrying elders like Uday Kotak.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora — itself set to transfer an estimated $4 trillion across generations — India's succession wave is a preview of how inherited wealth is being redeployed into global markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Indian Ateliers Stitching Dior, Prada and Gucci's Finest Pieces
articles.excerpt: Mumbai's Chanakya International employs 2,500 artisans for 30-plus luxury houses — but a row over Fendi's $10,000 Baguette has put the question of credit centre stage.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, the story reframes luxury shopping — the handwork behind a Dior or Fendi piece may well come from a Mumbai atelier, and credit for it is finally being claimed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Disclosed 1,156 July Trades, Including $25 Million Microsoft and Amazon Sales
articles.excerpt: The 37-page filing shows $79 million to $270 million in transactions — and a quick round-trip in two Big Tech names.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump at the White House. His latest financial disclosure lists 1,156 July securities transactions totaling between $79 million and $270 million.
articles.nri_angle: Indian investors holding US tech stocks through funds and brokerages are exposed to the same mega-cap names being rotated in the filing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bengaluru Startup's Hospital Music Night Sparks Backlash — and a Sequel
articles.excerpt: Superhealth founder Varun Dubey defended the August event as an attempt to build 'hospitals that don't scare people'; weeks later he announced a 'Bhajan Jam' at the same hospital.
articles.image_caption: Varun Dubey, founder and CEO of Superhealth Hospitals. Dubey publicly defended his startup after videos of a music night hosted inside its Bengaluru hospital drew online criticism last month.
articles.nri_angle: For Indians abroad who endure hospital visits back home as one of the most stressful parts of family emergencies, the episode is a cautionary tale about where the line sits between humanizing healthcare and trivializing the grief inside it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi High Court: NEET NRI Quota Can't Demand Guardianship Proof From Adult Candidates
articles.excerpt: Justice Jasmeet Singh held the Guardians and Wards Act applies to minors — and questioned the MCC's demand that NRI sponsors prove they "looked after" students as a subjective, case-by-case hurdle.
articles.image_caption: A stethoscope rests on examination papers in an illustration of the NEET, India's national medical entrance test. The Delhi High Court has held that adult candidates seeking admission under the NRI quota cannot be asked to produce a guardianship certificate.
articles.nri_angle: Directly affects NRI and OCI families sponsoring relatives for MBBS seats in India — the court's interim relief keeps the 15% NRI quota accessible without a slow court-ordered guardianship process.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Axar Patel Holds Nerve as India Survive Japan Scare in Historic Two-Run T20I Win
articles.excerpt: Rain reduced the historic one-off T20I in Sano to five overs a side, and 41st-ranked Japan came within two runs of stunning the T20 world champions before Axar Patel held his nerve in the final over.
articles.image_caption: India captain Shreyas Iyer (right) shakes hands with Japan captain Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming at the pre-match press conference in Sano. India went on to edge Japan by two runs in the rain-reduced one-off T20I, with the 41st-ranked hosts pushing the world champions to the final ball.
articles.nri_angle: Japan's cricketing rise is powered in part by players of Indian origin, making this historic first meeting between the sides a milestone for the diaspora's role in growing the game globally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BSF Stops Akal Takht Jathedar's Zero Line Ardas for Kartarpur Corridor Reopening
articles.excerpt: BSF stopped the Akal Takht Jathedar-led jatha from reaching the Zero Line at Dera Baba Nanak; the sangat held Rehras Sahib and ardas near the barricade as a Nagar Kirtan proceeded on the Pakistan side.
articles.image_caption: Sikh devotees gather near the border at Dera Baba Nanak. The Akal Takht Jathedar-led jatha was stopped by BSF from reaching the Zero Line on September 21, where it planned a special ardas seeking the Kartarpur Corridor's reopening.
articles.nri_angle: For the Sikh diaspora in the US, Canada and the UK, Kartarpur Sahib is a core pilgrimage site, and the visa-free corridor's suspension since May 2025 has cut off the practical route many families used around Gurpurabs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Starbucks Sets Up First India Tech Hub in Chennai, Plans 800 Tech Jobs
articles.excerpt: The coffee giant signed an MoU with Tamil Nadu for a corporate technology centre in Chennai's OMR corridor — a GCC for in-house software engineering, not stores — hiring in phases.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-origin technologists in the US weighing a move back, 800 in-house roles at a global brand in low-attrition Chennai widen the India tech-career corridor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Says He's in 'Deciding Mode' on Iran as Tehran Sends Terms via Qatar
articles.excerpt: The president outlined three paths — "wiping Iran out, letting them rot economically or making a deal" — while saying he would "probably" meet Iran's president at the UN General Assembly.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump said he is in 'deciding mode' on Iran as Tehran sent its terms via Qatar.
articles.nri_angle: Millions of Indians live and work in the Gulf states in the shadow of escalation, and surging energy prices hit India — the world's third-largest oil importer — hard, squeezing household budgets and remittance-dependent families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IndiGo Crew Member Kainoor Mistry Dies in Mumbai Cab Crash
articles.excerpt: The 32-year-old cabin crew member, a mother of an eight-year-old boy, died of head injuries after her airline-hired cab crashed on the Western Express Highway — renewing scrutiny of outsourced crew transport.
articles.image_caption: An IndiGo aircraft. Crew member Kainoor Mistry died in a cab crash in Mumbai.
articles.nri_angle: Aviation-crew safety and employer duty-of-care resonate across the diaspora — millions fly IndiGo and other Indian carriers, and many diaspora members work in aviation as crew, ground staff, and engineers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Who Is Vishal Sikka? The AI Pioneer Who Ran Infosys — and Just Raised $85 Million to Disrupt It
articles.excerpt: Nine years after a bruising exit from Infosys, the 59-year-old former SAP CTO has founded Hang Ten Systems, an enterprise AI startup that closed $85 million in seed funding in four months — with Intel and Micron's CEOs writing checks.
articles.image_caption: Vishal Sikka speaking at SAP's SAPPHIRE conference in Orlando in 2010, when he was the company's first-ever CTO. In 2026 he founded Hang Ten Systems, an enterprise AI startup that has raised $85 million in seed funding.
articles.nri_angle: Sikka's arc — small-town Madhya Pradesh to Stanford mentorship under AI's founding fathers to the top of Infosys and SAP, and now a founder again at 59 — embodies the Indian diaspora's outsize role in the AI era.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Bombay Director Signs 18-Point Charter, Apologises Amid Protests Over Student's Death
articles.excerpt: After a three-day sit-in over Sahil Wakode's death, Director Shireesh Kedare agreed to an independent probe and institutional reforms; the institute denied rumors of his resignation.
articles.image_caption: Prof. Shireesh Kedare, Director of IIT Bombay, who signed an 18-point charter of student demands amid protests over the death of second-year student Sahil Wakode.
articles.nri_angle: IIT Bombay is the alma mater of tens of thousands of Indian-origin engineers in the US — its governance, campus culture and handling of caste and mental-health issues are personal to the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cricket Frenzy Grips Indian and Pakistani Expatriates Across the Gulf
articles.excerpt: From Friday-morning games on Riyadh's open grounds to crowded restaurants during India-Pakistan clashes, cricket remains the cultural lifeline of South Asian expatriates — and Saudi Arabia is building a sporting future around it.
articles.image_caption: Sharjah Cricket Stadium, a popular venue for matches drawing large South Asian expatriate crowds in the Gulf. Cricket frenzy is gripping Indian and Pakistani expatriates across the Gulf.
articles.nri_angle: For millions of Indian and Pakistani workers in the Gulf, cricket is home in portable form — and Saudi Arabia's cricket push could soon give their children a national team of their own.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Conservatives Face Racial Gatekeeping From the MAGA Fringe
articles.excerpt: A Times of India report and U.S. coverage document racially charged attacks on Indian-American conservatives — from Ramaswamy's Ohio bid to Nikki Haley and JD Vance's family — even as immigration enforcement tightens around the community.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C. Indian-American conservatives say they face racial gatekeeping from parts of the MAGA movement.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-Americans across party lines are learning that political alignment does not shield them from racial gatekeeping — while immigration enforcement tightens around the community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: JioHotstar Goes Global: Ambani Targets Diaspora in UK, Canada, Singapore
articles.excerpt: JioHotstar replaces Hotstar in Britain, Canada and Singapore with 160,000+ hours of content across 12 languages — but no live sports at launch, and pricing runs about ten times Indian plans.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani's JioHotstar is expanding beyond India to target the diaspora in the UK, Canada and Singapore.
articles.nri_angle: JioHotstar's first overseas launch puts 160,000+ hours of Indian content in 12 languages directly in front of diaspora households in the UK, Canada and Singapore.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After Years in America, an NRI Came Home — and Felt He Didn't Belong
articles.excerpt: NDTV reported the account of an NRI who moved back after years in the United States and now describes loneliness and disconnection: "I feel like I don't belong here." The story reflects a wider, often unspoken strain among returning Indians.
articles.image_caption: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in Mumbai. After years in America, one NRI came home — and found he no longer felt he belonged.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs weighing a return, this story underscores that repatriation is an emotional transition as much as a logistical one — belonging must be rebuilt, not just revisited.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ChatGPT Helps Stranger Reunite Lost Punjab Elder With Family 1,200 Km Away
articles.excerpt: Chaman Lal, an elderly Ludhiana man with memory issues, vanished during an Amritsar pilgrimage and surfaced in Gaya, Bihar — until a stranger used ChatGPT to trace his village and escorted him home.
articles.image_caption: Gaya Junction railway station in Bihar. The missing elder surfaced in Gaya, roughly 1,200 km from his home in Ludhiana, before a local resident helped trace his family.
articles.nri_angle: Punjabi diaspora families, who manage ageing parents' care from abroad, share the specific anxiety of an elderly relative wandering off — making this both a cautionary tale and a reassurance about strangers' kindness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mandaviya Joins Indian Diaspora Cycle Ride to Cheer Asian Games Athletes
articles.excerpt: Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya cycled alongside members of the Indian community in Nagoya on Sunday as the diaspora rallied behind India's 500-strong contingent at the 20th Asian Games.
articles.image_caption: Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya joined the Indian diaspora in Nagoya for a Sundays on Cycle event on September 20, 2026. The community ride was organised to cheer for Indias contingent at the 20th Asian Games.
articles.nri_angle: The Nagoya ride showed the Indian diaspora in Japan turning out as volunteers and cheerleaders for the country's athletes on one of Asian sport's biggest stages.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala CM Satheesan Meets Jaishankar in Delhi, Flags NRI Welfare Priorities
articles.excerpt: V.D. Satheesan's meeting with the External Affairs Minister focused on consular assistance and grievance redressal for Non-Resident Keralites — his first major diaspora outreach as the state's new chief minister.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar (left) with Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan. The two leaders met in New Delhi on Saturday to discuss welfare measures for the Non-Resident Keralite community.
articles.nri_angle: The meeting puts Pravasi welfare at the center of the new Kerala government's agenda, with consular help and grievance redressal for Keralites abroad now a direct CM-to-EAM channel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: London NRI With Rs 38 Crore Asks: Is FatFIRE Realistic in a Tier-1 Indian City?
articles.excerpt: A London-based NRI's viral Reddit question about retiring early in India has reignited the debate over what financial independence really costs in cities like Bengaluru — and whether even a Rs 38 crore corpus is enough.
articles.image_caption: A hand stacks coins against a backdrop of stock market charts. The article examines whether a Rs 38 crore corpus is enough for FatFIRE in a Tier-1 Indian city like Bengaluru.
articles.nri_angle: The story captures the reverse-migration dilemma facing wealthy NRIs: whether a large foreign-earned corpus buys genuine financial independence back home once Bengaluru's real costs, taxes and healthcare risks are factored in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
